note: RETROSPECTIVE 2026-09-04 (lane R13; findings A12#0/#1/#2/#8, A9#5): every line was re-diagnosed against the committed baselines and re-measured with the shipping metric stack (padToCanvas → pixelmatch 0.02/includeAA:false → ssim.js fast → CIEDE2000 stride 4 → classifyDivergence, exactly compare-screenshots.mjs diffPair); `observed` is that re-measurement, `observedAt` its date, `observedFrom` its provenance. The seed's 'corner AA' story was WRONG for 14 lines: the visible divergence is a CLIP asymmetry (iOS clips in-flow content to the rounded shape; both natives clip under background-image layers; Android drops descendant ink under blur), and the seed's 'edgeSSIM 1.00' was the then-broken all-ones metric. `owner` is a lane/mechanism handle (platform-category-mechanism), never a person. Lines whose fix is in flight are marked EXPECTED STALE: exit 5 at the next gate names them and the only action is DELETE. Expiry decisions are written into each reason. ORIGINAL SEED NOTE FOLLOWS. Known cross-platform divergences on fixtures/visual-test.json, seeded from a live three-platform run (327 pairs, 23 failing at SSIM<0.95 || dpx>2%). A LEDGER, not a tolerance: each line names one divergence, why it is believed benign or why it is a bug, who owns it, and when it must be re-reviewed. Deleting a line is how a fix gets recorded. READ THIS: 6 of these entries are REAL SIZE BUGS surfaced for the first time by the magenta pad sentinel - before that fix a short render was padded with the capture background and scored a perfect diff. They carry a short expiry because they need fixing, not excusing. Of the remainder, almost all fail on SSIM alone with dpx well under the 2% budget and deltaE95 = 0.00 - the colours are exact and SSIM is scoring curve/transform anti-aliasing. That is evidence about the METRIC, not the runtimes, and most of those lines should evaporate when the gate moves off SSIM. ALSO measured on composition-test.json (2026-08-26): pixelmatch at threshold 0.25 reported pixelMismatchedPct 0.00 for 037_Nested_OpacityGroup while 36.63% of pixels differ by up to 80 per channel. Its YIQ budget is 0.25*35215 = 8803.8, and a PURE LIGHTNESS shift must exceed 132/255 to be counted — so black (0,0,0) vs mid-grey (130,130,130) is reported as identical. The 2% pixel gate therefore cannot fire on any uniform lightness error smaller than half the dynamic range. Only SSIM (0.9355) and deltaE95 (20.94) caught this row. KEYS ARE INDEX-FREE: entries store the component NAME without the capture's {NNN}_ prefix, because that prefix is a position in the flattened capture list and renumbers whenever the corpus changes. WAVE 50 (2026-09-15, device gate wave50-final): the gate reported 17 of these lines STALE (`now passing, delete the line`) — 9 of the 10 ios-borders-radius lines (retro R4 clip fix confirmed on device; Edge_InsetRoundShadow iOS-Android stays, it still diverges), the 2 android-effects-blur lines (retro R6) and the 6 android-harness-placeholder-floor lines (wave-50 lane B11) — and they were DELETED per the exit-5 contract. 27 -> 10 lines. WAVE 51 PR 3 (2026-09-22, the harness label as capture-frame chrome): the refresh MEASURE run (BASELINE=1 on the fixed harnesses, before any refresh) reported the 2 Edge_GradientWithRadius lines (Android-web, iOS-web) STALE at SSIM 0.9995 / 0.9996, dpx 0.00 — their reason was the web label painted past the rounded box, and no platform paints a label inside the box any more — DELETED per the exit-5 contract. 12 -> 10 lines.

expectations.reason: NOT a runtime gap — CORRECTED 2026-08-28. backdrop-filter IS implemented on both natives (docs/STATUS.md wave 26: a two-pass controlled-canvas model, validated on iOS against browser refs at 0.966 / 0.978 / 0.999, edge model later corrected against Chrome). What the control measured is a CAPTURE-MODE gate, not a missing applier: the two-pass path arms only on the COMPOSED capture path and is deliberately disarmed on the per-component path this fixture runs through. Android: `wantsBackdropPass = composedMode && documentDeclaresBackdropFilter(composed)` (ScreenshotCaptureScreen.kt:309). iOS: ScreenshotCaptureView states it outright — 'Lane BF-I deliberately does NOT two-pass here... the WPT paths below, where a backdrop element actually has neighbours, are where the two-pass runs.' Both disarm to keep the committed 327-pair baselines byte-identical. THE REAL GAP: composition-test.json was authored precisely so backdrop-filter has a non-uniform backdrop, and test-all.sh has no way to arm composed capture, so the ordinary fixture pipeline cannot exercise the property on either native. That is a harness gap to close, not a runtime bug to fix. NOTE this correction was made from source comments and the STATUS wave-26 record; I did not re-run composed mode to confirm it end to end. RE-REVIEWED 2026-09-04 (retro R13): no committed baselines exist for composition-test.json and the documented gate never runs it, so this line is INERT — neither exit 4 nor exit 5 can reach it — until the gate script adds `BASELINE=1 ./test-all.sh fixtures/composition-test.json` (retro A9#5). expectations.reason: iOS CLIP ASYMMETRY, not corner AA (re-diagnosed 2026-09-04, retro A12#0; the seed's 'edgeSSIM 1.00' was the then-broken all-ones metric). runtimes/swiftui/Sources/StyleConverterRuntime/StyleEngine/borders/radius/BorderRadiusApplier.swift applied `.clipShape(BorderRadiusShape)` UNCONDITIONALLY, so iOS clips in-flow content — here the block-font label — to the rounded box while Android and web paint it past the box edge. css-backgrounds-3 §4.3 (Corner Clipping) bounds the element's OWN background and border painting at the curve; descendants are clipped only when overflow is not visible (css-overflow-3 §3.1, the clip rounded per §3.1.2). Committed baselines, ink right of x=80 (pixels more than 40/255 from the ground in any channel): iOS 0 px vs Android 257 / web 257; dE95 0.00 because every surviving pixel is the right colour, and the Android-web pair of this component PASSES — rasteriser AA would separate Android from web too. Android's twin was fixed wave 41 T5 (BorderRadiusApplier.kt selfPaintsWithoutClip). FIX IN FLIGHT: retro R4 gates the iOS clip behind clipsDescendants (self-paint + .contentShape while overflow is visible). EXPECTED STALE at the next visual-test gate: exit 5 names this line — the action is DELETE, never re-add. CAVEAT for this pair: re-measured dpx is 3.218% (over the 2% budget) with dE95 1.13 — the inset-shadow band also differs (CoreGraphics-vs-Skia sigma, the mechanism of the Android-web line), so the pair may survive the clip fix on dpx alone. Re-measure at the gate; if it still fails, re-ledger it under ios-effects-shadow-inset with the new numbers instead of carrying this line.

expectations.reason: iOS renders translucent `sepia()` with a plain source-over composite. FilterApplier.swift's sepia branch builds `ZStack { v; v.colorMultiply(reweight).grayscale(1).colorMultiply(tint).opacity(a) }` — exact for OPAQUE content (7 of the 8 rows in this fixture land on the CSS value) and wrong when the element's own alpha < 1, because `.opacity(a)` multiplies the top layer's alpha: coverage A comes out A*a + (1-A*a)*A rather than A. On rgba(52,152,219,0.5) under sepia(80%) over the #1A1A2E stage the arithmetic is 0.4*(178.7,159.2,124.0) + 0.6*(0.5*(52,152,219) + 0.5*(26,26,46)) = (94.9,117.1,129.1) -> rgb(95,117,129), against the spec/web/Android rgb(90,92,95). The alternative was tried and reverted: complementary opacities with .plusLighter inside a .compositingGroup fixes this row and stops SwiftUI Text being filtered at all (white text under sepia(80%) came out (255,255,255) where spec/web/Android give (255,255,242)); fixtures/properties/effects/filter-on-text.json pins that trade. RE-LEDGERED 2026-09-15 (wave-50 post-gate iOS fix lane), and the mechanism is NOT a new regression — this is the same divergence the two lines deleted at 747b28e4 described. What changed is the MEASUREMENT: retro lane R13 re-scored this row from the COMMITTED BASELINE PNGs (ledger-remeasure.json: 'NOW-PASSING(STALE)', ssim 0.9979 / 0.9986) and deleted both lines, but tools/visual/baseline/iOS__006_Sepia_Translucent.png is itself stale — its box is rgb(89,92,95), i.e. the REVERTED .plusLighter additive render (0.5*(0.2c + 0.8*Sc) + 0.5*ground = (89.7,91.9,94.5)), which no shipping FilterApplier produces. Executed this lane on Catalyst (ImageRenderer scale 1 through a byte-mirror of the harness CaptureCanvas, proven byte-identical to the simulator captures on 7 other components): the live render is rgb(95,117,129) x4559 px and differs from that committed iOS baseline by 4800 px / 17.094% at max channel delta 34 — exactly the gate's dpx and the oracle waiver's dmax. Reverting wave-50 lane B8's StyleBuilder `.engineVisibility` reorder on a scratch copy left the raster byte-identical, and 5aa92ed6..747b28e4 touches SepiaMatrix.swift and BoxShadowApplier.swift in COMMENT lines only, so no render moved in that range. The row was invisible until now because tools/visual/gate-fixtures.txt — the fixture set the gate iterates — was itself created at 747b28e4; before it the gate ran fixtures/visual-test.json alone and this fixture was never executed. SEPARATE AND STILL OPEN: the stale iOS baseline makes this component report REGRESSION (exit 1) until it is refreshed with UPDATE_BASELINE=1 — that refresh is the orchestrator's, not this ledger's. Delete these lines when the iOS sepia composite preserves alpha without flattening Text.
